  Number Theory and Cryptography [CSE-3111]  
  Marks: 50                                                                               Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1)           Compute all congruence classes of Modulo 8  
  Illustrate extended Euclidian algorithm for finding the inverse of 12 mod 79  
  (5)  
  A)  
  B)      a. Calculate phi(n) for n = 1200 and n = 2008.  
  b. Let n 2 N and let p be a prime. Show that if p|n then phi(n*p) = p*phi(n).              (5)  
  
  2)           Prove that n13 - n is divisible by 2, 3, 5, 7, and 13 for any integer n.  
  (5)  
  A)  
  B)      Let 'm' be an odd integer and let 'a' be any integer. Prove that 2m +2 a can never be a  
  perfect square.                                                                            (5)  
  
  3)           Find the remainder when 2100 + 3100 + 4100 + ............+10100 is divide by 11.  
  (5)  
  A)  
  B)      Let X be a nonempty set. Show that the power set R = 2X together with the set  
  $$operations of symmetric difference A + B = (A ∩ B͞ ) U (B ∩ A͞ ) and intersection AB =     (5)$$  
  A∩B, is a ring. Is R commutative? Does it have unity? Justify  
  
  4)           Encrypt the message "meet me at the usual place at ten rather than eight o clock" using  
  $$the Hill cipher with the key=$$  
  a. Show your calculations and the result.                                                  (5)  
  A)  
  b. Show the calculations for the corresponding decryption of the ciphertext to recover  
  the original plaintext.  
  
  B)      Using the Vigenere cipher, encrypt the word "cryptographic" using the word "mit".  
  Analyse the efficiency of mono & poly alphabetic cipher                                    (5)  
  
  5)           Consider the system which uses highly simplified DES Algorithm with Iteration-4            (5)  
  output as "1A037825BD81C028" (hex). Compute Iteration-5 using the key as  
  "13902B148936" (hex).
